title: THE VOTE OF THE UPLIFTED GOATS
deck: Forty goats in a dale byre have voted, unanimously, for something nobody can name, and a sale is about to fence off the hill; Illuminara spends two evenings in the straw until she hears what the vote is a translation of, and lets the herd correct her answer.
shape: Seven scenes across eleven days: a byre meeting, a bedtime counting game, a back room of the dale registry, a correction in the straw, a conversation at a pasture gate, a dawn climb with the whole herd, and the sitting of the assembly.

scenes.title: The Byre
paragraphs: *Marrick Farm, Brannoch Dale · evening, eleven days before the sitting*

The goats had called the meeting, and Odile Marrick wanted that understood before anything else. They had called it by walking into the byre at dusk, all forty, and standing in the straw in the patient way of animals who have listened to people for a long time. A veterinary trial that went wrong eleven years ago had left them able to follow an argument. It had not left them quick about it.

**Odile**  
They voted last Tuesday. Forty on the left side of the byre, and then eleven walked across to the right and back again, and the vet wrote that down as a recount. I think it was a joke.

**Illuminara**  
What did they vote for?
Odile held out the vet's notepad. It carried three phrases, copied down over three nights: *the hill*, *the count*, *the going-up*.

**Odile**  
The assembly sits in eleven days to decide whether they are livestock or residents. The cooperative has voted to sell the high pasture, as one lot, through a Mr Pruett, to people who want to put cabins on it. I have been asked to bring the goats' position, and I do not have one. I have three phrases.

**Illuminara**  
Why did you send for me?

**Odile**  
Because I am afraid of being wrong in either direction. Call them persons and the assembly may take them from a farm that loves them. Call them stock and I have said exactly what the sale needs me to say. And I will not hand forty living creatures to a court on the strength of what a goat said in a barn.
At the far end of the byre an old nanny with a grey muzzle got up out of the straw, one leg at a time, and came the length of the floor. The others made room without being asked.

**Bracken**  
You are the one who listens. Sit. Sit down. Down in the straw.
Illuminara sat. It seemed to be the first item of business, and the sigh that went through the herd told her she had guessed right.

scenes.title: The Count
paragraphs: *The byre · the second evening*

Illuminara spent two evenings in the byre before she asked anyone anything. She had asked Odile to come without her clipboard, and Odile sat on an upturned bucket by the door with an expression somewhere between suspicion and relief.

She ate what the kids ate, which was oat cake pressed with something bitter and green, and found she liked it, and that the kids found her liking it very funny. She learned that the herd did not so much talk as take turns: one word, then a pause long enough to hold a whole thought, then another. She learned that a goat in conversation says the same thing three times, so that nobody has to ask twice. She had also noticed, without quite noticing, that every time one of the three phrases was spoken the whole herd leaned a little toward the east door.
At bedtime the kids played a game. One said a name, the next said it again and added another, and so on down the straw, and a small brown kid with one folded ear always got furthest.

**Tansy**  
Byre Gate. Split Ash. Byre Gate, Split Ash, the Wet Step. Byre Gate, Split Ash, the Wet Step, Tolly's Rise.

**Illuminara**  
What is the game called?

**Tansy**  
The count.
She said it the way a child says *the alphabet*. Illuminara sat very still, because something in her head had come loose and she did not want to knock it off the shelf.
*Not goats. Places.*

**Illuminara**  
Tansy, what comes after Tolly's Rise?

Fourteen names came out of the straw in order, ending at a place called the Long Look. The vet had written down three demands. They were one. The hill was where the rhyme went. The count was the rhyme. The going-up was the walking of it.

**Illuminara**  
Who taught you the count?

**Tansy**  
Bracken. Bracken's mother. Bracken's mother's mother. The count.

scenes.title: The Registry
paragraphs: *The Brannoch Dale registry, back room · the fourth morning*

The registrar listened to Odile without a word and then wheeled out a flat drawer. The enclosure award of 1844 was a map the colour of weak tea, and across the high ground ran a dotted line labelled in a hand like barbed wire: *Common Way, as anciently used, for the going-up and coming-down of beasts to the common grazing above the Lamb Wall.* Fourteen waymarks were pencilled along it. Illuminara read them aloud, once, and Odile sat down on a box of ledgers.

**Odile**  
Split Ash. Tolly's Rise. My grandfather said that in the lambing shed. I thought it was a nursery rhyme.

**Illuminara**  
It is a survey. The award only wrote down a road that was already old. They have been saying the bounds of it since before the ink, and calling it a game, because nobody else was listening.

**Odile**  
Then why is it not in Pruett's title?

**Registrar**  
Because there are two ledgers. The award book keeps a right alive by an entry, and nothing else. A holder's claim is an entry. A walk that I or a holder sets down is an entry. Twenty years with none, and the right lapses. Pruett's title is drawn from the parcel index, and the index carries only what a holder has entered against a parcel. The last entry in the award book is nineteen years old, a lambing-week walk my predecessor happened to see. Nobody has ever entered the Way against the land.

**Illuminara**  
So the right is alive in one book and invisible in the other. The herd has kept the road alive on foot, and the paper has let it go quiet. Eleven months left on the clock.

**Registrar**  
And a goat cannot lodge a claim. The sale particulars were drawn from the index as it stands.
He slid a second sheet across the desk. It offered the high pasture as an unencumbered single lot.

**Odile**  
So I enter a claim for the holding, and the Way goes onto the title before the lot is divided, and the sale cannot close as written. But to do that I must say it is the holding's herd that uses it. Which is the word they did not want said. A thing people do to them.

**Illuminara**  
Yes. I could draft it tonight, and it would be correct, and it would win. I think we ask first.

**Odile**  
Ask whom?

**Illuminara**  
The people whose road it is.

scenes.title: The Correction
paragraphs: *The byre · that night*

She laid it out the slow way, a sentence and then a wait, for as long as it took. The way was in the award. The right belonged to the holding. The cooperative would claim it, the herd's going-up would stand as the use, and forty goats would keep the hill without anyone having to rule on what they were.
It was a good plan. She was a little proud of it, and had not hidden that well. Bracken heard it out to the end. Then she said, three times over, the word Illuminara had hoped not to hear.

**Bracken**  
No. No. No.

**Illuminara**  
Tell me where it is wrong.

**Bracken**  
For these forty. Forty die, the way is gone. Not for us. For the kids who are not yet. For whoever the herd is.

Illuminara's pride went out of her all at once, and what came in behind it was more useful. She had written the right for the animals in front of her. The herd had asked for a road that would outlast them.

**Illuminara**  
The right runs with the herd, whoever it is. Kids born, strays taken in. Not forty names.

**Bracken**  
Good. And a road to a shut gate is no road. The grass at the end of it is the end of the road. We want the hearing. When the way changes, the cooperative counts us first. We say. We say before.

**Odile**  
You want a veto over my own land?

**Bracken**  
Over the road. Not the farm. The road is the road.

**Odile**  
And where it goes?

**Bracken**  
A road goes somewhere.
Odile looked at the old nanny for a long time. Then she looked at the straw, where Tansy lay asleep with her mouth still moving on the count.

**Odile**  
Then the sale loses the top of the hill. The grass above the Lamb Wall stays in the cooperative's name, out of every lot, and I put that to people who voted for the whole of it. I will write more than you asked. Neither the Way nor the grass it goes to can ever be sold, and nothing on either is changed without your speakers heard first. Not in a bad year. Not ever.

**Bracken**  
That is more than we asked. Good. It is not enough. A road no one walks is a road in a drawer. The way must be walked. Every spring. Kids at the front. If it is walked and the book sees it, it is used. If it is used, it is not lost. The hill remembers if we walk.

Illuminara wrote that down and understood what Bracken had just done. The right had come within eleven months of lapsing because nobody could claim it. It would not come near again, because the entry was a morning walk the herd would make whether or not anyone asked, and the registrar had only to be there to see it.

scenes.title: The Gate
paragraphs: *The high pasture gate · afternoon, four days before the sitting*

Mr Hale Pruett was not a villain, which Illuminara found inconvenient. He was a tidy man in a waterproof the colour of porridge, acting for a buyer who had paid a deposit, with a lender who wanted a clean title behind her, and the look of someone who has read a great many documents carefully and is now being shown one that was not in the file. He had read the award twice.

**Pruett**  
You are asking my client to accept, for ever, forty goats walking through his scheme twice a year, on the strength of a nursery rhyme.

**Illuminara**  
On the strength of an award, which the rhyme matches stone by stone. I walked the line last night with my palm flat on the air. The old groove is still there under the gorse, four hundred years of the same weight on the same line.

**Pruett**  
And the lot is halved.

**Illuminara**  
It is. The grass above the Lamb Wall leaves the sale. Your client keeps the lower meadow, the road frontage, the water, and seven of his eleven plots. The Way is a four-metre lane along the wall, outside the plots, mapped and entered on the title on the first day instead of found by your lender's solicitor in March.

**Pruett**  
The price falls.

**Illuminara**  
It does. She will lend against a lane she can read. She cannot lend against a claim in the registrar's drawer that nobody has told her about.

**Pruett**  
And if the goats change their minds?

**Illuminara**  
Then they say so, in the count, to the cooperative, before anything moves. It is the only change to that lane you will ever have to deal with, and it will come with notice.
He looked up the hill for a while.

**Pruett**  
My guests will ask what the noise is.

**Illuminara**  
Twice a year, a fine one. Bring your lender to the walk.

**Pruett**  
I agree to nothing. I will carry a mapped lane, seven plots and a walk to my client, and they will say what they say.
He wrote *spring walk, autumn walk* in the margin of the particulars, which is how a careful man marks what he expects to have to defend.

scenes.title: The Going-Up
paragraphs: *The Common Way · dawn, the morning of the sitting*
They went up in the grey: forty goats, the whole membership of the cooperative and the registrar with a notebook, and Tansy at the front, because the kids go first.

**Tansy**  
Byre Gate, Split Ash, the Wet Step, Tolly's Rise, the Lamb Wall.

At the Wet Step she stopped, put one hoof in the water to prove it was wet, and went on, and forty animals lifted their feet over the same stones in the same order. A hollow the width of a goat ran through the gorse under the frost. Odile walked at the back with her hands in her pockets, saying the names under her breath and getting two of them wrong. The registrar walked beside the kids and wrote, after each waymark, a line.

Pruett had come, in the porridge-coloured waterproof, with his phone in his hand. At the Lamb Wall he stood and looked at it while the herd went past him, and then he read aloud, to nobody, a message that had come in at five.

**Pruett**  
From my client. Seven good plots and a story no other cabins in the county have, beats eleven plots and a lawsuit. Sign it.

He dialled the other number. Illuminara, last in the line, heard only his half, which was enough: *Yes. A registered lane. Seven plots. The ground above the wall out of the sale.* A long listening. *Forty. The kids go first.* Another. He laughed once, unwillingly.

**Pruett**  
She will lend against a lane on the title, not against a surprise. And she wants to know whether they walk on Sundays.

Illuminara walked last of all, and was surprised by how much she minded being last. She had decoded a rhyme and found a map and lost an argument to a goat, and none of it had felt like this: a hill being gone up by those it belonged to, one name at a time, at the speed of the smallest.

At the Long Look Bracken stopped, and the herd stopped behind her. The whole dale lay below them in the first sun with its roofs smoking, and the registrar closed his notebook on the first entry of the next twenty years.

**Bracken**  
Now the hill knows who is coming.

**Tansy**  
Again?

**Bracken**  
Again. Next spring. And the spring after.

scenes.title: What the Assembly Left Open
paragraphs: *Brannoch Dale assembly hall · noon*

The assembly's question was whether forty goats were livestock or residents, and it spent an hour discovering that it had not been asked the right one. Odile Marrick stood up with no notes. She said the cooperative was not asking for a category. It was claiming the Common Way in the award of 1844 for its holding, with that morning's walk entered in the award book as use and the claim entered against the title before the lot was divided. It was covenanting that neither the Way nor the grass it went to would ever be sold, and that nothing on either would change until the herd's chosen speakers had been heard. She had filed the covenant that morning, with a hoof-print inked beside her signature, because Bracken had insisted on a mark.

The chair asked whether this decided what the goats were. Odile said it decided what they could count on. The assembly adjourned the other question, as she had hoped, and nobody much minded, since the hill was no longer for sale in the form that had made the question urgent. The cooperative kept the high pasture above the Lamb Wall in its own name, and the herd would go on grazing it as it always had, on ground the cooperative had bound itself never to sell. Pruett's client signed the amendment at the gate before ten: the lower meadow and seven plots, at a lower price, with the lane along the wall written into the title as the Common Way, and a lender who asked only that the spring walk be put in the brochure.

It cost something. Two members of the cooperative resigned that week, one of them a man who had wanted the sale money and who would not forgive Odile for choosing the goats' road over his drains. The question of what the herd was remained open, and Bracken's speakers would have to defend the covenant at the count for years.

That night in the byre Tansy said the count, the whole fourteen, and did not lose a name. Illuminara found she was saying it with her, under her breath, the way and not the goats. Odile stood in the doorway with the cooperative's book and no clipboard, and when the last name was done she wrote under the date, in her small square hand, *Count taken.*

critic_line: Illuminara learns that the herd's vote is a living survey and refuses to file the easy answer until Bracken corrects it; the goats retain a walked, registered road and its high pasture, while the cooperative, buyer and lender freely accept a smaller durable bargain with its costs disclosed.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1; genuine independent GPT and Claude judgments; exact equal 50/50 arithmetic mean.
shared_strengths: The twist that the goats' vote is a rhyme which is really a land survey is charming and idea-driven, and the dialogue is humane. The legal and registry mechanics in the middle are dense and the negotiation is neat, which may lose some readers. Bracken's correction and the closing walk are memorable.

The premise fits perfectly, the dialogue gives the goats dignity without sentimentality, and the count's conversion from nursery rhyme to legal map supplies a satisfying intellectual and emotional payoff. Some readers may slow at the registry mechanics, but the concrete stakes, dry humor, and recurring road imagery carry the story through.
shared_reservations: The award book keeps a right alive by an entry, and nothing else. A holder's claim is an entry. A walk that I or a holder sets down is an entry. Twenty years with none, and the right lapses.

translation_sl.title: GLASOVANJE POVZDIGNJENIH KOZ
translation_sl.deck: Štirideset koz v hlevu v dolini je soglasno glasovalo za nekaj, česar nihče ne zna poimenovati, prodaja pa bo kmalu ogradila hrib; Illuminara preživi dva večera v slami, dokler ne zasliši, kaj glasovanje prevaja, in dovoli čredi, da popravi njen odgovor.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v enajstih dneh: sestanek v hlevu, večerna igra štetja, zadnja soba dolinskega registra, popravek v slami, pogovor pri pašniških vratih, jutranji vzpon s celotno čredo in zasedanje skupščine.

scenes.title: Hlev
paragraphs: *Kmetija Marrick, dolina Brannoch · večer, enajst dni pred zasedanjem*

Sestanek so sklicale koze in Odile Marrick je hotela, da se to razume še pred vsem drugim. Sklicale so ga tako, da je vseh štirideset ob mraku vstopilo v hlev in obstalo v slami na potrpežljiv način živali, ki ljudi poslušajo že dolgo. Veterinarski poskus, ki je šel pred enajstimi leti narobe, jim je omogočil slediti argumentu. Ni pa jim podaril hitrosti.

**Odile**  
Glasovale so prejšnji torek. Vseh štirideset na levi strani hleva, nato pa jih je enajst prešlo na desno in nazaj, veterinar pa je to zapisal kot ponovno štetje. Mislim, da je bila šala.

**Illuminara**  
Za kaj so glasovale?
Odile ji je podala veterinarjevo beležnico. V njej so bile tri zveze, prepisane v treh nočeh: *hrib*, *štetje*, *vzpenjanje*.

**Odile**  
Skupščina zaseda čez enajst dni, da odloči, ali so živina ali prebivalke. Zadruga je glasovala za prodajo visokega pašnika kot ene parcele prek gospoda Pruetta ljudem, ki želijo na njem postaviti koče. Prosili so me, naj predstavim stališče koz, jaz pa ga nimam. Imam tri zveze.

**Illuminara**  
Zakaj ste poslali pome?

**Odile**  
Ker me je strah, da se bom zmotila v eno ali drugo smer. Če jim rečem osebe, jih lahko skupščina vzame kmetiji, ki jih ima rada. Če jim rečem živina, sem povedala natanko to, kar potrebuje prodaja. In štiridesetih živih bitij ne bom izročila sodišču na podlagi tega, kar je koza rekla v hlevu.
Na skrajnem koncu hleva je iz slame vstala stara koza s sivim gobcem, eno nogo za drugo, in prehodila vso dolžino poda. Druge so ji naredile prostor, ne da bi jih kdo prosil.

**Bracken**  
Ti poslušaš. Sedi. Sedi dol. V slamo.
Illuminara je sedla. Videti je bilo, da je to prva točka dnevnega reda, vzdih, ki je šel skozi čredo, pa ji je povedal, da je pravilno uganila.

scenes.title: Štetje
paragraphs: *Hlev · drugi večer*

Illuminara je v hlevu preživela dva večera, preden je kogarkoli karkoli vprašala. Odile je prosila, naj pride brez svoje podloge za papir, zato je Odile sedela na obrnjenem vedru pri vratih z izrazom nekje med sumničavostjo in olajšanjem.

Jedla je, kar so jedli kozlički: ovseno pogačo, stisnjeno z nečim grenkim in zelenim. Ugotovila je, da ji je všeč, kozličkom pa se je zdelo zelo zabavno, da ji je všeč. Spoznala je, da čreda ne govori toliko, kolikor si jemlje besedo: ena beseda, nato dovolj dolg premor za celo misel, nato druga. Spoznala je, da koza v pogovoru isto stvar pove trikrat, da nikomur ni treba vprašati dvakrat. Opazila je tudi, ne da bi zares opazila, da se je ob vsaki od treh zvez vsa čreda nekoliko nagnila proti vzhodnim vratom.

Pred spanjem so se kozlički igrali igro. Eden je izrekel ime, naslednji ga je ponovil in dodal še eno, in tako naprej po slami; majhen rjav kozliček z enim prepognjenim uhljem je vedno prišel najdlje.

**Tansy**  
Hlevska vrata. Razcepljeni jesen. Hlevska vrata, Razcepljeni jesen, Mokra stopnica. Hlevska vrata, Razcepljeni jesen, Mokra stopnica, Tollyjev vzpon.

**Illuminara**  
Kako se igra imenuje?

**Tansy**  
Štetje.
Izgovorila je tako, kakor otrok reče *abeceda*. Illuminara je sedela povsem pri miru, ker se ji je nekaj v glavi sprostilo in ni hotela, da pade s police.
*Ne koze. Kraji.*

**Illuminara**  
Tansy, kaj pride za Tollyjevim vzponom?

Iz slame je po vrsti prišlo štirinajst imen, zadnje za kraj, ki se je imenoval Dolgi razgled. Veterinar je zapisal tri zahteve. Bile so ena sama. Hrib je bil tam, kamor je vodila izštevanka. Štetje je bilo izštevanka. Vzpenjanje je bilo njeno prehojenje.

**Illuminara**  
Kdo te je naučil štetja?

**Tansy**  
Bracken. Bracknina mati. Mati Bracknine matere. Štetje.

scenes.title: Register
paragraphs: *Register doline Brannoch, zadnja soba · četrto jutro*

Matičar je Odile poslušal brez besed, nato pa izvlekel ploski predal. Zemljevid iz odločbe o ograditvi iz leta 1844 je bil barve šibkega čaja, čez visoki svet pa je tekla pikčasta črta z napisom v pisavi, podobni bodeči žici: *Skupna pot, kakor se uporablja od davnine, za vzpenjanje in spuščanje živine do skupne paše nad Jagnječjim zidom.* Ob njej je bilo s svinčnikom označenih štirinajst mejnikov. Illuminara jih je enkrat prebrala na glas, Odile pa je sedla na zaboj z glavnimi knjigami.

**Odile**  
Razcepljeni jesen. Tollyjev vzpon. Moj ded je to govoril v jagnjetnici. Mislila sem, da je otroška izštevanka.

**Illuminara**  
To je popis. Odločba je le zapisala pot, ki je bila stara že takrat. Njene meje izgovarjajo že od časa pred črnilom in temu pravijo igra, ker jih nihče drug ni poslušal.

**Odile**  
Zakaj je potem ni v Pruettovem naslovu?

**Matičar**  
Ker sta dve glavni knjigi. Knjiga odločbe ohrani pravico živo z vpisom in z ničimer drugim. Zahtevek imetnika je vpis. Hoja, ki jo vpišem jaz ali imetnik, je vpis. Dvajset let brez enega in pravica ugasne. Pruettov naslov je vzet iz parcelnega registra, ta pa vsebuje le tisto, kar je imetnik vpisal ob parceli. Zadnji vpis v knjigi odločbe je star devetnajst let, hoja med tednom jagnjitev, ki jo je po naključju videl moj predhodnik. Poti ni še nihče vpisal ob zemljišče.

**Illuminara**  
Pravica je torej živa v eni knjigi in nevidna v drugi. Čreda je pot ohranila živo z nogami, papir pa jo je pustil utihniti. Na uri je ostalo enajst mesecev.

**Matičar**  
Koza pa zahtevka ne more vložiti. Prodajni pogoji so bili sestavljeni po registru, kakršen je.
Čez mizo je potisnil drugi list. Visoki pašnik je ponujal kot neobremenjeno enotno parcelo.

**Odile**  
Torej vložim zahtevek za posestvo, Pot se vpiše v naslov, preden se parcela razdeli, prodaja pa se ne more končati, kakor je zapisana. Toda za to moram reči, da jo uporablja čreda posestva. To je beseda, ki je niso hotele slišati. Nekaj, kar jim ljudje naredijo.

**Illuminara**  
Da. Lahko bi zahtevek pripravila nocoj, bil bi pravilen in zmagal bi. Mislim, da najprej vprašamo.

**Odile**  
Koga?

**Illuminara**  
Tiste, katerih pot je.

scenes.title: Popravek
paragraphs: *Hlev · tisto noč*

Razložila je počasi: stavek in nato čakanje, kolikor dolgo je bilo potrebno. Pot je bila v odločbi. Pravica je pripadala posestvu. Zadruga bi jo uveljavila, vzpenjanje črede bi veljalo kot uporaba in štirideset koz bi obdržalo hrib, ne da bi moral kdorkoli razsoditi, kaj so.
Načrt je bil dober. Bila je malce ponosna nanj in tega ni najbolje skrivala. Bracken ga je poslušala do konca. Nato je trikrat izrekla besedo, za katero je Illuminara upala, da je ne bo slišala.

**Bracken**  
Ne. Ne. Ne.

**Illuminara**  
Povej mi, kje je napačen.

**Bracken**  
Za teh štirideset. Štirideset jih umre, poti ni več. Ne za nas. Za kozličke, ki jih še ni. Za kogarkoli, ki je čreda.
Illuminarin ponos je iz nje ugasnil naenkrat, kar ga je nadomestilo, pa je bilo uporabnejše. Pravico je zapisala za živali pred seboj. Čreda je prosila za pot, ki jih bo preživela.

**Illuminara**  
Pravica pripada čredi, kdorkoli jo sestavlja. Rojeni kozlički, sprejeti potepuhi. Ne štirideset imen.

**Bracken**  
Dobro. Pot do zaprtih vrat pa ni pot. Trava na njenem koncu je konec poti. Hočemo zaslišanje. Ko se pot spremeni, nas zadruga prešteje prve. Mi povemo. Povemo prej.

**Odile**  
Hočete veto nad mojo zemljo?

**Bracken**  
Nad potjo. Ne nad kmetijo. Pot je pot.

**Odile**  
In nad tem, kamor vodi?

**Bracken**  
Pot nekam vodi.
Odile je dolgo gledala staro kozo. Nato je pogledala v slamo, kjer je Tansy spala, usta pa so se ji še vedno premikala ob štetju.

**Odile**  
Potem prodaja izgubi vrh hriba. Trava nad Jagnječjim zidom ostane v lasti zadruge, zunaj vsake parcele, in to bom predložila ljudem, ki so glasovali za celoto. Zapisala bom več, kot ste zahtevale. Niti Pot niti trava, h kateri vodi, ne smeta biti nikoli prodani, na nobeni od njiju pa se nič ne spremeni, ne da bi prej zaslišali vaše govorke. Ne v slabem letu. Nikoli.

**Bracken**  
To je več, kot smo zahtevale. Dobro. Ni dovolj. Pot, po kateri nihče ne hodi, je pot v predalu. Po poti je treba hoditi. Vsako pomlad. Kozlički spredaj. Če je prehojena in jo knjiga vidi, je uporabljena. Če je uporabljena, se ne izgubi. Hrib si zapomni, če hodimo.

Illuminara je to zapisala in razumela, kaj je Bracken pravkar naredila. Pravica je prišla na enajst mesecev do ugasnitve, ker je nihče ni mogel uveljaviti. Nikoli več se ji ne bo tako približala, saj bo vpis jutranja hoja, ki jo bo čreda opravila, ne glede na to, ali jo kdo prosi, matičar pa bo moral biti le tam, da jo vidi.

scenes.title: Vrata
paragraphs: *Vrata visokega pašnika · popoldne, štiri dni pred zasedanjem*

Gospod Hale Pruett ni bil zlikovec, kar se je Illuminari zdelo neprijetno. Bil je urejen mož v nepremočljivi jakni barve ovsene kaše, zastopnik kupca, ki je plačal aro, s posojilodajalko, ki je za njim želela čist naslov, in z videzom človeka, ki je skrbno prebral veliko dokumentov, zdaj pa mu kažejo enega, ki ga ni bilo v spisu. Odločbo je prebral dvakrat.

**Pruett**  
Mojo stranko prosite, naj za vedno sprejme štirideset koz, ki dvakrat letno hodijo skozi njegov projekt, na podlagi otroške izštevanke.

**Illuminara**  
Na podlagi odločbe, ki se z izštevanko ujema kamen za kamnom. Sinoči sem prehodila črto z dlanjo plosko v zraku. Stara brazda je še vedno tam pod uleksom, štiristo let iste teže na isti črti.

**Pruett**  
Parcela pa je prepolovljena.

**Illuminara**  
Je. Trava nad Jagnječjim zidom se umakne iz prodaje. Vaša stranka obdrži spodnji travnik, dostop do ceste, vodo in sedem od enajstih parcel. Pot je štiri metre širok pas ob zidu, zunaj parcel, kartiran in vpisan v naslov prvi dan, namesto da ga marca odkrije odvetnica vaše posojilodajalke.

**Pruett**  
Cena pade.

**Illuminara**  
Pade. Posodila bo proti poti, ki jo lahko prebere. Ne more posoditi proti zahtevku v matičarjevem predalu, o katerem ji ni nihče povedal.

**Pruett**  
Kaj pa, če si koze premislijo?

**Illuminara**  
Potem to s štetjem povedo zadrugi, preden se karkoli premakne. To je edina sprememba te poti, s katero boste kadarkoli imeli opravka, in prišla bo z obvestilom.
Nekaj časa je gledal v hrib.

**Pruett**  
Moji gostje bodo spraševali, kaj je ta hrup.

**Illuminara**  
Dvakrat letno bo lep. Pripeljite posojilodajalko na hojo.

**Pruett**  
Z ničimer ne soglašam. Kartirano pot, sedem parcel in hojo bom predstavil svoji stranki, oni pa bodo povedali svoje.
Na rob prodajnih pogojev je zapisal *spomladanska hoja, jesenska hoja*, tako pa skrben človek označi tisto, za kar pričakuje, da bo moral zagovarjati.

scenes.title: Vzpenjanje
paragraphs: *Skupna pot · zora, jutro zasedanja*
V sivo jutro so se vzpenjali: štirideset koz, celotno članstvo zadruge in matičar z beležnico, Tansy pa spredaj, ker gredo kozlički prvi.

**Tansy**  
Hlevska vrata, Razcepljeni jesen, Mokra stopnica, Tollyjev vzpon, Jagnječji zid.

Pri Mokri stopnici se je ustavila, položila eno kopito v vodo, da bi dokazala, da je mokra, in nadaljevala; štirideset živali je dvignilo noge čez iste kamne v istem vrstnem redu. V uleksu je pod slano tekla vdolbina, široka kakor koza. Odile je hodila zadaj z rokami v žepih, si potiho ponavljala imena in dve izgovorila narobe. Matičar je hodil ob kozličkih in po vsakem mejniku zapisal vrstico.

Pruett je prišel v nepremočljivi jakni barve ovsene kaše in s telefonom v roki. Pri Jagnječjem zidu je obstal in ga gledal, medtem ko je čreda hodila mimo njega, nato pa je na glas, nikomur posebej, prebral sporočilo, ki je prišlo ob petih.

**Pruett**  
Od moje stranke. Sedem dobrih parcel in zgodba, kakršne nima nobena druga koča v okrožju, je boljše od enajstih parcel in tožbe. Podpišite.

Poklical je drugo številko. Illuminara, zadnja v vrsti, je slišala le njegovo polovico, kar je zadoščalo: *Da. Vpisana pot. Sedem parcel. Zemljišče nad zidom zunaj prodaje.* Dolgo poslušanje. *Štirideset. Kozlički gredo prvi.* Še eno. Enkrat se je nehote zasmejal.

**Pruett**  
Posodila bo proti poti v naslovu, ne proti presenečenju. In vedeti želi, ali hodijo ob nedeljah.

Illuminara je hodila čisto zadnja in presenetilo jo je, kako zelo jo je motilo biti zadnja. Razvozlala je izštevanko, našla zemljevid in izgubila argument s kozo, toda nič od tega se ni zdelo tako: hrib, po katerem se vzpenjajo tisti, ki jim pripada, eno ime za drugim, s hitrostjo najmanjšega.

Pri Dolgem razgledu se je Bracken ustavila, za njo pa čreda. Vsa dolina je ležala pod njimi v prvem soncu, iz streh se je kadilo, matičar pa je zaprl beležnico nad prvim vpisom naslednjih dvajsetih let.

**Bracken**  
Zdaj hrib ve, kdo prihaja.

**Tansy**  
Spet?

**Bracken**  
Spet. Naslednjo pomlad. In pomlad za njo.

scenes.title: Kar je skupščina pustila odprto
paragraphs: *Skupščinska dvorana doline Brannoch · opoldne*

Vprašanje skupščine je bilo, ali je štirideset koz živina ali prebivalke, in porabila je uro, da je odkrila, da ji niso postavili pravega vprašanja. Odile Marrick je vstala brez zapiskov. Povedala je, da zadruga ne prosi za kategorijo. Uveljavlja Skupno pot iz odločbe iz leta 1844 za svoje posestvo; jutranja hoja je bila v knjigo odločbe vpisana kot uporaba, zahtevek pa je bil vpisan ob naslovu, preden se je parcela razdelila. Zavezala se je, da niti Pot niti trava, h kateri vodi, ne bosta nikoli prodani in da se na nobeni nič ne bo spremenilo, dokler ne bodo zaslišane govorke, ki jih izbere čreda. Zavezo je vložila tisto jutro, z odtisom kopita ob svojem podpisu, ker je Bracken vztrajala pri znamenju.

Predsedujoči je vprašal, ali to odloča, kaj so koze. Odile je odgovorila, da odloča, na kaj se lahko zanesejo. Skupščina je drugo vprašanje preložila, kakor je upala, in to ni nikogar posebej motilo, saj hrib ni bil več naprodaj v obliki, zaradi katere je bilo vprašanje nujno. Zadruga je visoki pašnik nad Jagnječjim zidom obdržala v svojem imenu, čreda pa se bo na njem pasla naprej, kakor se je vedno, na zemljišču, za katero se je zadruga zavezala, da ga ne bo nikoli prodala. Pruettova stranka je spremembo podpisala pri vratih pred deseto: spodnji travnik in sedem parcel po nižji ceni, s pasom ob zidu, zapisanim v naslovu kot Skupna pot, in posojilodajalko, ki je zahtevala le, naj bo spomladanska hoja navedena v brošuri.

Nekaj je stalo. Tisti teden sta iz zadruge izstopila dva člana; eden je želel denar od prodaje in Odile ni mogel odpustiti, da je izbrala pot koz namesto njegovih odtokov. Vprašanje, kaj je čreda, je ostalo odprto, Bracknine govorke pa bodo morale zavezo ob štetju braniti še leta.

Tisto noč je Tansy v hlevu povedala celotno štetje, vseh štirinajst imen, in ni izgubila niti enega. Illuminara je ugotovila, da ga govori z njo, potiho, pot in ne koze. Odile je stala pri vratih z zadružno knjigo in brez podloge za papir; ko je bilo izrečeno zadnje ime, je pod datumom s svojo majhno oglato pisavo zapisala: *Štetje opravljeno.*

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara spozna, da je glasovanje črede živ popis, in noče vložiti lahkega odgovora, dokler je Bracken ne popravi; koze obdržijo prehojeno, vpisano pot in njen visoki pašnik, zadruga, kupec in posojilodajalec pa svobodno sprejmejo manjši, trajen dogovor z razkritimi stroški.
